Map paragraphs, headings, marks, links, breaks, separators, lists, quotes and code to shared schema primitives. Preserve code whitespace, list nesting/order, checked state, link destinations and alt text. Map images/tables only through registered portable descriptors with explicit fallback behavior. The v1 optional content descriptors use existing opaque block tuples, tagged `module:editac.image` or `module:editac.table`, followed by version 1 and bounded JSON data. This does not change profile roots or the v5 wire schema. Known descriptors validate before staging; disabled/unknown descriptors retain source and inert text. Images retain URL/alt/title/source without a network request. Tables retain alignment, rectangular rows and rich simple-cell runs (32 columns, 128 rows, 1,024 runs, 1 MiB text/source). SFR-1.1 admits semantic LF inside both v1 and v2 runs, retaining the existing version tags, mark/link policy and bounds. Enter and Shift+Enter within one editable cell both insert LF; they do not add rows or cell blocks. Shared table commands/descriptors reject CR rather than silently rewriting it. Native textarea input and the explicit literal clipboard action normalize external CRLF/CR to LF before preparation; tabs and all other scalar text remain literal. Ill-formed UTF-16 rejects at the browser boundary before conversion. Exact expected tuples pin delayed edits, and unchanged/cancelled/rejected preparation creates no history. Markdown exports supported cell LFs as attribute-free `
` (including empty, repeated and trailing breaks), and imports only the shared finite inert `br` allowlist with the active marks. Physical table rows and source line endings are separate from cell LFs. Unsupported Markdown marks (including multiline inline code) retain explicit diagnostics and exact typed descriptor/source recovery; no lossy Markdown fallback is qualified as exact. Single-block cell selection copy offers the internal run matrix and literal HTML/quoted TSV (also used for plain text); quoting retains embedded LF, tabs and quotes. Multi-block cells retain only the structured flavor, preserving distinct block boundaries. Existing descriptor source bytes remain retained verbatim when editing cells; semantic export never overwrites them. Inline image layout and nested cell containers remain explicit unsupported source fallbacks. Registration governs activation; rendering/upload services remain separately owned.

WEB-1.9 provides atomic internal fragments, the bounded safe HTML adapter, literal/minimal-host text policy, optional reachable plain-paste control and platform plain-paste shortcuts. Full Rust CommonMark/GFM import and configurable formatted plain-text policy retain their parser qualification gates and FMT-1.13 integration owner. Registered codecs provide additional MIME/asset/extension support; RTF and image/file clipboard items require declared typed/resource-bounded adapters rather than pretending binary items are text. EXT-1.13 and RCH-1.23 own formatting-preserving table cells, captions and other extension payloads, with native and mobile presenter tasks and separate physical or virtual platform gates. The supported palette is the admitted model/codec capability set; unavailable formats retain inert source with diagnostics. Literal paste retains destination formatting but never imports source formatting or parses Markdown/HTML.

Both recovered `mountEditor` and borrowed-engine `mountEditorSurface` accept `preset`, `plainTextPolicy`, `contentCodecs` and `typingShortcuts`. Original REG-05 binds canonical left-aligned v5 paragraphs: their existing `["paragraph"]` tuple is the actual left presentation, without a new schema/root or table-cell metadata. The native prepared block command `setAlignment { owner, alignment: "left" }` validates a visible paragraph and preserves its presentation, source spans, text and marks. The existing v5 `insertParagraph` command beside a separator captures a right-affine result caret at the end of the newly staged paragraph's authored UTF-16 text. Capture occurs in preparation after creation/placement, so later commands rebase the relative anchor and rejection has no live effects. Explicit final `selectionAt` retains precedence. This result maps through the production DOM bridge; an exact DOM selection of a noneditable block is a node action, never an adjacent text range. Separator node deletion uses one prepared native command with a right-affine resulting adjacent text caret: the previous editable owner’s UTF-16 end, otherwise the next editable owner’s start; if neither exists, it creates one empty paragraph and returns its start. Explicit final `selectionAt` retains precedence; unsupported textual node actions reject without overwriting neighbors. These policies do not qualify table-specific or native gesture/device behavior.
